newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close up ahead of expected rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close up ahead of expected rate cut.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed higher on Wednesday, supported by bond market advances amid widespread expectations of a key rate cut at Thursday's repo.
However the fact that the market is still characterised by a lack of final investors advises caution, dealers said.
The general index rose 1.73 points, 0.47 percent to 371.83 and the Ibex added 22.68 points, 0.53 percent, to 4,262.39.
Energy firm Repsol added 50 pesetas to 4,365 on a technical rebound after a period of prolonged weakness, with European oil sector gains also adding to the effect, dealers said.
The Bank of Spain is widely expected to cut its key money rate by 25-50 basis points at Thursday's repo, and views are mixed on how the bourse would take either move.
"The market is expecting a cut, which if less than 50 basis points could produce some sales," said one dealer. In any case, a 50 basis point move could prompt profit-taking, he added.
Stocks would probably take their lead from bonds after the repo, dealers said.
